findings.source_passage: all her spars thickly clustering with men... the boastful sails all fell together as blank bladders that are burst, and all life fled from the smitten hull
findings.why_it_matters: The simile 'blank bladders that are burst' and 'all life fled from the smitten hull' is a prosodically distinctive opening image that establishes the chapter's ominous register; only the clustering-men detail survives.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'blank bladders that are burst / all life fled from the smitten hull' simile in the opening paragraph.

findings.source_passage: ere her commander, who, with trumpet to mouth, stood up in his boat; ere he could hopefully hail, Ahab's voice was heard
findings.why_it_matters: The syntactic suspension ('ere … ere') and the detail of the trumpet-to-mouth commander shape the chapter's dramatic rhythm; Ahab cutting off any greeting before it begins is an interpretive moment of his monomania.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'ere her commander, with trumpet to mouth … ere he could hopefully hail' construction to preserve both the rhetorical rhythm and the interpretive beat.

findings.source_passage: "He's drowned with the rest on 'em, last night," said the old Manx sailor standing behind them; "I heard; all of ye heard their spirits."
findings.source_locator: after Stubb's cry 'We must save that boy'
findings.why_it_matters: The Manxman's uncanny line is a signature moment of the novel's supernaturalism and his role as dread prophet; its omission erases a critical voice-establishing beat in the middle of the chapter.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert the Manxman's line verbatim after Stubb's 'We must save that boy.'

findings.source_passage: a little lad, but twelve years old, whose father with the earnest but unmisgiving hardihood of a Nantucketer's paternal love, had thus early sought to initiate him in the perils and wonders of a vocation almost immemorially the destiny of all his race
findings.source_locator: paragraph on the fuller backstory of the Rachel's captain
findings.why_it_matters: This passage supplies the chapter's moral and cultural texture—Nantucket custom, father-son vocation, paternal love—that makes Ahab's refusal so devastating; the draft reduces it to 'the missing boy was but twelve.'
findings.suggested_fix: Expand the backstory paragraph to include 'unmisgiving hardihood of a Nantucketer's paternal love' and the idea that the boy was sent early to learn the whaleman's vocation.

findings.source_passage: leaving the strange captain transfixed at this unconditional and utter rejection of his so earnest suit. But starting from his enchantment, Gardiner silently hurried to the side; more fell than stepped into his boat
findings.why_it_matters: 'Transfixed … unconditional and utter rejection … starting from his enchantment' is rhythmically distinctive and interpretively loaded (Gardiner as spell-struck); the draft collapses it to 'started from his trance.'
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'transfixed at this unconditional and utter rejection of his so earnest suit' and 'starting from his enchantment' for the closing action beat.

summary: Three medium-severity losses—the 'blank bladders' opening simile, the Manxman's ghost-prophet line, and the Nantucket-paternal-love passage—combine with the erasure of the 'ere … ere' rhetorical suspension to constitute sufficient signature damage to require regeneration.
